[RDSC.5a.2] **Triple-driven backend selection.** The
compiler reads each observation triple
(aggregation × time-model × accuracy) declared on the
series, groups triples by compatible backings per
[LSER.18.1],
coalesces shared backings, and emits exactly the backend
atoms needed. The wire shapes below name the v1 backings
the matrix maps to:

- `SeriesBackendWelfordEwma` — Welford running stats. Selected for
  every aggregation [LSER.18.1] backs with it on `all_time`
  (cumulative semantics). v1 is cumulative-only.
- `SeriesBackendRingBuffer` — exact ring buffer. Selected for any
  aggregation on `sliding <dur>` whose triple admits
  exact backing per the matrix.
- `SeriesBackendMonotonicDeque` — monotonic deque. Selected for **exact** `min` / `max`
  on `sliding`.
- `SeriesBackendFifoDeque` — FIFO deque. Selected for `first` / `bool_and` /
  `bool_or` on `sliding`.
- `SeriesBackendReservoir` — reservoir. Selected for the bag aggregations on the
  `sample <n>` time model; `max_samples` carries `n`.
- `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse` — interval pulse ([RDSC.5a.9]). Selected for
  `active_fraction` on `sliding` ([LSIG.1.1]).
- `SeriesBackendNumericIntegral` — numeric integral ([RDSC.5a.10]). Selected for
  `integral` on `sliding` and `all_time` ([LSIG.1.1]).

Every quantile / cardinality /
membership / top-k need defers to the exact `SeriesBackendRingBuffer` bag.

The matrix is the source of truth for triple → backend
selection; the wire shapes below are stable, but the
selection rules summarised here are illustrative and
evolve with the matrix.

**A backing no rule reads is not emitted.** The compiler **may** omit a backing
that serves no aggregation a rule reads, whether or not the series' other
backings are read, and a series no rule reads emits no backend atom at all.
Such a series has no meaning: nothing but a rule
reads a series ([NSBK.6.3]).
